/-!
# Erdős Problem 212

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/212](https://www.erdosproblems.com/212)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos212

/--
Is there a dense subset of ℝ^2 such that all pairwise distances
are rational?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_212 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ u : Set ℂ, Dense u ∧ u.Pairwise fun c₁ c₂ => dist c₁ c₂ ∈ Set.range Rat.cast := by sorry

end Erdos212

reformulations.difference: The Euclidean plane is represented by ℂ, and rational distances are required only for distinct points through Set.Pairwise.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Complex.orthonormalBasisOneI.repr is an isometric equivalence between ℂ and EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), so transporting sets preserves density and all distances. Set.range Rat.cast here is precisely the rational numbers embedded in ℝ. Including equal points adds only distance 0, which is rational. The full equivalence with a dense subset of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) whose distances between all pairs are rational was proved as Review212.euclidean_plane_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorry or dependence on the conjecture.
